A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VI-Net research. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–C are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 experiments, including accuracy, throughput, truncation and pruning studies, and intrinsic-dimension analysis.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and reports revised baseline results in the truncation comparisons.

M1.justification: The VI-Net pipeline, generator construction, pruning, and fine-tuning remain unchanged. The tanh restriction mentioned in v2 Section 4.2 was already implemented and described in v1 Section 3.2 and Appendix C.4.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-10 and CIFAR-100 image classification with ResNet-based models. No datasets, tasks, domains, or distinct test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the full ResNet baselines, Linear Head, Random Monomials, and ABM/OAVI variants using Frank-Wolfe or accelerated gradient descent. The new linear-probing citation does not introduce another evaluated comparator.

E3.justification: The stated settings remain unchanged, including 128-dimensional PCA, maximum degree 5, vanishing tolerance 0.1, and SGD settings. Appendix A.2.1 retains 512 training images per class and 20 retraining epochs. The revised plots are not accompanied by a reported protocol change.

E4.justification: Figures 3 and 5 revise evidence in the existing truncation ablations comparing linear heads, random monomials, and learned polynomial features. The questions tested remain the same, and the pruning, generator-choice, and intrinsic-dimension analyses in Appendix A.2.2–A.2.8 are retained.

E5.justification: Table 2 continues to report throughput averaged over five random seeds with standard deviations. No repeated-run counts, uncertainty-reporting practices, or significance tests are added or revised.

E6.justification: Figure 3 substantially revises the CIFAR-100 Linear Head curve: at about 76% layer removal, accuracy changes from approximately 7% to 50%, sharply narrowing VI-Net's advantage. Zero-truncation baseline values also change in Figures 3 and 5; Figure 5 raises Random Monomials from about 46% to 93% and slightly adjusts the other initial points. Tables 1–2 and Figures 4 and 6–12 retain their results.

T1.justification: Definition 4.3 corrects the binomial term defining j_k from 'i choose d' to 'd choose i'. Section 4.2 explicitly connects the bounded latent-output domain to the analysis, although that restriction already appeared in Lemma B.4. The principal theorem statements and appendix proofs are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, four stated contributions, and conclusion retain the same core claims: algebraically characterize latent manifolds, construct efficient VI-Nets with competitive accuracy, and obtain potential spectral-complexity and generalization advantages.

C2.justification: A new introductory footnote distinguishes algebraic varieties from manifolds related to them by diffeomorphism. Section 4.2 replaces the earlier norm-comparison explanation with guidance on selecting polynomial hyperparameters. Appendix B adds the limitation that weight norms lack an a priori bound; the existing overlap and high-dimensionality limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds a code-repository URL at the beginning of Section 5. This supplies access information absent from v1; the implementation details and experimental hyperparameters in Section 5.1 and Appendices A and C are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Alain and Bengio (2016) to position VI-Net relative to linear probing, and Pokutta et al. (2020) and Zimmer et al. (2025) for bounded-norm training. Other reference changes mainly update publication details of already cited works.

P1.justification: V2 makes localized introduction and theory edits, adds Problem 2.1 restating the existing objective, and adds a generic Impact Statement. Author and publication information also changes, while the overall section and appendix organization remains intact.

P2.justification: Figures 3 and 5 are redrawn with revised colors, markers, legends, and axis formatting, including a different accuracy-axis range in Figure 3. Figure 4 is relocated, and the title page and tables reflow. The figure and table inventory remains unchanged.

improvement.justification: The corrected binomial term, clearer theoretical scope and limitations, and added code-access pointer modestly improve mathematical precision and reproducibility information. The substantial baseline revisions in Figures 3 and 5 are unexplained, so they do not establish better experimental quality. The supported overall gain is limited.
